S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.

subtypes.Intrusive Memories: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Distressing Dreams: Recurrent distressing dreams in which the content and/or affect of the dream are related to the traumatic event.
subtypes.Dissociative Reactions (Flashbacks): Dissociative reactions (e.g., flashbacks) in which the individual feels or acts as if the traumatic event were recurring.
subtypes.Psychological Distress at Cues: Intense or prolonged psychological distress at exposure to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.
subtypes.Physiological Reactions to Cues: Marked physiological reactions to internal or external cues that symbolize or resemble an aspect of the traumatic event.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.

subtypes.Internal Avoidance: Efforts to avoid distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings about or closely associated with the traumatic event.
subtypes.External Avoidance: Efforts to avoid external reminders (people, places, conversations, activities, objects, situations) that arouse distressing memories, thoughts, or feelings.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).

subtypes.Fragmented Memory: Inability to recall only specific parts of the traumatic event while remembering others.
subtypes.Generalized Amnesia: Inability to recall the majority or the entirety of the traumatic event.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.

subtypes.Negative Self-Beliefs: Distorted beliefs such as 'I am fundamentally bad,' 'I am damaged,' or 'I am worthless'.
subtypes.Negative Beliefs about Others: Distorted beliefs such as 'No one can be trusted' or 'Others are dangerous'.
subtypes.Negative Worldview: Extreme beliefs such as 'The world is completely dangerous' or 'Life is meaningless'.

S073.name: Distorted_Cognitions_With_Blame
S073.description: Persistent, distorted cognitions about the cause or consequences of the traumatic event that lead the individual to blame himself/herself or others.

subtypes.Self-Blame: Blaming oneself for the occurrence of the trauma or for not preventing it.
subtypes.Blaming Others: Distorting the situation to blame specific others for the occurrence or damage of the trauma.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.

subtypes.Impulsive Anger: Sudden explosions of anger for trivial reasons or no clear reason.
subtypes.Verbal Aggression: Attacking others with shouting, cursing, or blame without holding back.
subtypes.Physical Aggression: Physically attacking people or throwing/breaking objects.
subtypes.Chronic Irritability: A state where nerves are always sharp and sensitive, ready to explode at the slightest touch.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.

subtypes.Scanning for Danger: Always scanning the surroundings and being alert to find potential threats or risks.
subtypes.Safety Checking: Repetitively confirming safety, such as checking exit locations or observing people around.
subtypes.Sustained Alertness: Unable to relax tension even in safe environments and maintaining a constant state of alertness.

symptom.disease_info: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) is a trauma- and stressor-related disorder that develops after exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence, either directly, as a witness, or through learning about events affecting close others. It is characterized by persistent re-experiencing of the trauma, avoidance of trauma-related stimuli, negative alterations in cognitions and mood, and marked changes in arousal and reactivity lasting more than one month and causing functional impairment. The clinical course can be acute or chronic, with some individuals developing delayed onset or experiencing waxing and waning severity over years. PTSD is distinguished from other anxiety and mood disorders by the requirement of a qualifying traumatic event and the specific pattern of trauma-linked intrusions, avoidance, and hyperarousal.

patient.personality: Joseph is a meticulous, community-oriented retiree who enjoys structured routines, hands-on projects, and sharing local history, while tending to worry over small details.
patient.stressor: Just over two years ago, Joseph was driving his teenage grandson home from a fishing trip when another vehicle lost control on an icy Minnesota back road and struck them head-on, causing their car to roll into a ditch; Joseph was conscious throughout, trapped in the driver’s seat, unable to reach his grandson, who died before paramedics arrived. The combination of profound grief, the shock of suddenly losing a beloved family member in such a violent and unexpected way, and his belief that he should have foreseen the danger or not driven in those conditions deeply unsettled his previously stable, detail-focused world. In the months after the accident he tried to maintain his volunteer roles at the senior center and church, but his usual pleasure in gardening, woodworking, and community events was overshadowed by a persistent sense of threat and a need to constantly check his surroundings and the well-being of others, even in familiar settings like bingo nights or the library. As his preoccupation with safety and his jumpiness in crowds began to interfere with his ability to coordinate volunteers and even sit through church services, his pastor and daughter encouraged him to see a psychiatrist to address the lingering aftereffects of the crash and his ongoing difficulty feeling at ease anywhere.
patient.chief_complaint: “Ever since the accident, I feel on edge all the time, like I'm always bracing for something terrible to happen.”

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I lie there for hours replaying the drive home instead of falling asleep, and when I finally do drift off I wake up two or three times from the same kind of dream where we're back on that icy road, so even if I’m in bed all night I get up feeling wrung out instead of rested.

S069.name: Intrusive_Symptoms
S069.description: Recurrent, involuntary, and intrusive distressing memories of the traumatic event.
S069.manifestation: It hits me out of nowhere—like when I hear tires squeal or see a car swerve on the news—and suddenly I’m back in that ditch, smelling the gasoline and hearing my grandson gurgling, and for a few seconds it doesn’t feel like a memory, it feels like it’s happening again and my chest just clamps up.

S070.name: Trauma_Avoidance
S070.description: Persistent avoidance of stimuli associated with the traumatic event.
S070.manifestation: I go out of my way to avoid that stretch of road, winter driving in general, even riding in the passenger seat with my daughter, and I change the channel or leave the room if there’s a car crash on TV because the second I let my mind go there I feel like I’m going to fall apart.

S071.name: Trauma_Related_Amnesia
S071.description: Inability to remember an important aspect of the traumatic event (typically due to dissociative amnesia and not to other factors like head injury or alcohol).
S071.manifestation: What bothers me is there are whole chunks of the accident I just can’t pull up—like I know the car rolled and I remember being trapped and hearing him, but I can’t for the life of me picture the actual impact or how many times we flipped, it’s just a blank spot that won’t fill in no matter how hard I try.

S072.name: Negative_Beliefs
S072.description: Persistent and exaggerated negative beliefs or expectations about oneself, others, or the world.
S072.manifestation: Ever since the crash I walk around thinking the world isn’t really safe and that I’m the kind of person who’ll miss something important and get his own grandson killed, so I second-guess every decision and have a hard time believing anything good will last.

S073.name: Distorted_Cognitions_With_Blame
S073.description: Persistent, distorted cognitions about the cause or consequences of the traumatic event that lead the individual to blame himself/herself or others.
S073.manifestation: I keep going over that day and telling myself that if I’d checked the weather one more time, or taken the main highway instead of that back road, or just canceled the trip, he’d still be here, so in my head it feels like his death is on me even when my family tells me it was just a freak accident.

S077.name: Irritability_Aggression
S077.description: Irritable behavior and angry outbursts (with little or no provocation) typically expressed as verbal or physical aggression.
S077.manifestation: I used to be pretty even-tempered, but now I find myself snapping at my daughter for being five minutes late or barking at folks at the senior center if they don’t follow the safety rules I’ve posted, and afterward I feel ashamed because I know I overreacted but in the moment I’m just boiling over.

S079.name: Hypervigilance
S079.description: Persistent state of being alert and tense about the surrounding environment.
S079.manifestation: Whether I’m at church, the grocery store, or just sitting in my living room, I’m constantly watching the doors, checking who’s coming and going, listening for screeching brakes outside, and I can’t seem to let my guard down long enough to just relax and enjoy things the way I used to.
